ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC<BC$, and $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$ and intersects $AB$ at point $D$. A circle $\odot O$ is drawn with $DB$ as the diameter, which intersects $CD$ and $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$ respectively. Connect $BE$ and $EF$. What is the degree measure of $\angle EBF$? If $DE=DC$ and $BC=8$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect DF and construct EG$\perp$BF at point G,\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and CD bisects $\angle ACB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCB= \frac{1}{2} \angle ACB=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ BD is the diameter of circle $O$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFB=\angle DEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CFD=180^\circ-\angle DFB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle FDC=\angle FCD=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EBF=180^\circ-\angle EDF=\angle FDC=45^\circ$;\\
$\because$ $\angle CEB=90^\circ$ and $\angle EBC=\angle ECB=45^\circ$, BC=8, DE=DC,\\
$\therefore$ CE=BE,\\
$\therefore$ CG=BG= $\frac{1}{2}$ BC=4,\\
$\therefore$ EG= $\frac{1}{2}$ BC=4,\\
$\because$ $\angle CFD=\angle CGE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ DF$\parallel$EG,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{FG}{FC}=\frac{DE}{DC} =1$,\\
$\therefore$ FG=FC= $\frac{1}{2}$ CG=2,\\
$\therefore$ EF= $\sqrt{EG^2+FG^2}=\sqrt{4^2+2^2}=\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.

In cyclic quadrilateral D-E-B-F, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠EBF=180°−∠EDF. Since ED and DC are opposite rays on the same line, this equals ∠FDC=45°. Therefore ∠EBF=45°. For the length EF, construct EG⊥BF with G on BF. Since E, D, C are collinear and ∠DEB=90°, we get ∠CEB=90°. Also ∠ECB=45°, so triangle CEB is a 45°-45°-90° triangle with hypotenuse CB=8. Thus its altitude to the hypotenuse gives CG=BG=4 and EG=4. Since DF⊥BF and EG⊥BF, DF∥EG. In triangle CEG, DE=DC means D is the midpoint of CE; the line through D parallel to EG meets CG at F, so F is the midpoint of CG. Hence FC=FG=2. In right triangle EFG, EF=√(EG²+FG²)=√(4²+2²)=√20=2√5.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC<BC$, and $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$ and intersects $AB$ at point $D$. A circle $\odot O$ is drawn with $DB$ as the diameter, which intersects $CD$ and $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$ respectively. Connect $BE$ and $EF$. What is the degree measure of $\angle EBF$? If $DE=DC$ and $BC=8$, what is the length of $EF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $DF$ and construct $EG\perp BF$ at point $G$.\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $BD$ is the diameter of circle $O$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFB=\angle DEB=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CFD=180^\circ-\angle DFB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle FDC=\angle FCD=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EBF=180^\circ-\angle EDF=\angle FDC=45^\circ$;\\
$\because$ $\angle CEB=90^\circ$ and $\angle EBC=\angle ECB=45^\circ$, $BC=8$, $DE=DC$,\\
$\therefore$ $CE=BE$,\\
$\therefore$ $CG=BG=\frac{1}{2}BC=4$,\\
$\therefore$ $EG=\frac{1}{2}BC=4$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CFD=\angle CGE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $DF\parallel EG$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{FG}{FC}=\frac{DE}{DC}=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $FG=FC=\frac{1}{2}CG=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $EF=\sqrt{EG^2+FG^2}=\sqrt{4^2+2^2}=\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a right triangle ABC with C at the lower left, AC vertical upward to A, and CB horizontal to the right ending at B. Segment AB is slanted, and CD is a diagonal angle-bisector from C meeting AB at D, then continuing to E. A circle is drawn through D, E, F, and B, with O on DB, indicating DB is the diameter. Point F lies on CB, and segments BE and EF are drawn. Reasoning: Since ∠ACB=90° and CD bisects ∠ACB, we have ∠DCB=45°. Because DB is the diameter of the circle, by Thales' theorem ∠DFB=90° and ∠DEB=90°. Since C, F, B are collinear, ∠CFD=90°. In triangle CDF, ∠DCF=45° and ∠CFD=90°, so ∠FDC=45°. In cyclic quadrilateral D-E-B-F, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠EBF=180°−∠EDF. Since ED and DC are opposite rays on the same line, this equals ∠FDC=45°. Therefore ∠EBF=45°. For the length EF, construct EG⊥BF with G on BF. Since E, D, C are collinear and ∠DEB=90°, we get ∠CEB=90°. Also ∠ECB=45°, so triangle CEB is a 45°-45°-90° triangle with hypotenuse CB=8. Thus its altitude to the hypotenuse gives CG=BG=4 and EG=4. Since DF⊥BF and EG⊥BF, DF∥EG. In triangle CEG, DE=DC means D is the midpoint of CE; the line through D parallel to EG meets CG at F, so F is the midpoint of CG. Hence FC=FG=2. In right triangle EFG, EF=√(EG²+FG²)=√(4²+2²)=√20=2√5.
